Wastewater Enterprise Quarterly Report Including Southeast Area Major Projects Update (1) Biosolids, (2) Headworks, and (3) 1550 Evans Southeast Community Center
items.text: Wastewater Enterprise (WWE) Quarterly Report Including Southeast Area Major Projects Update (1) Biosolids, (2) Headworks, and (3) 1550 Evans Southeast Community Center Stephen Robinson, WWE Capital Programs Director, outline the overall project status and provided brief construction updates on: (1) Sunset Green Infrastructure Project (anticipated completion September 2021), (2) Mariposa Dry-Weather Pump Station and Force Main improvements (anticipated completion December 2022), and Southeast Plant (SEP) Power Feed and Primary Switchgear Upgrades (anticipated completion June 2024). He reviewed the Phase I status for the 70 projects in the Sewer System Improvement Program (SSIP) stating that as of March 2021 Phase I is 44.7% complete with 17 projects in construction. He discussed the SSIP cost summary and the facilities and infrastructure status cost summary. Director Robinson touched on capital programs highlights and reviewed: (1) project status for the Southeast Plant (SEP) Biosolids Digester Facilities Project. He stated that recent bids came in higher than expected and that the SFPUC suspended bid procurement activities to reassess bidding and the project delivery approach; (2) SEP New Headworks Facility Project. He noted a conflict with PG&E regarding and overhead cable around the western side of the facility (art wall) and stated that talks are taking place to resolve the conflict; and (3) Southeast Community Center 550 Evans, with hopes of earlier occupancy than expecte

Authorize the General Manager to execute a Memorandum of Understanding with the San Francisco Airport Commission
items.text: Authorize the General Manager to execute a Memorandum of Understanding with the San Francisco Airport Commission in an amount not-to-exceed $3,800,000 with a term of one year and 11 months, for SFPUC to fund consulting services and engineering design work for the development and environmental review of the Electric Capacity Upgrade Program to increase capacity and improve redundancy at the two SFPUC- owned airport substations, Airport Substation and Substation MA. Barbara Hale, AGM Power, stated the MOU will support the Airport with their improvements and will allow the SFPUC to help coordinate consulting services for electrical capacity upgrades

items.title: Authorize the General Manager to execute Memoranda of Understanding with San Francisco Public Works (SFPW) for the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission’s use of a portion of SFPW property
items.text: Authorize the General Manager to execute Memoranda of Understanding No-4453 and No-4454 with San Francisco Public Works (SFPW) for the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission’s use of a portion of SFPW property, located at 2323 Cesar Chavez Street in San Francisco, to construct a sewer tunnel and appurtenant facilities for the Kansas and Marin Streets Sewer Improvements Project, and for related temporary construction staging for a period of 20 months, with an option to extend for six months, at no cost to the SFPUC. Derek Adams, Project Manager, stated this is Phase II of the project and noted the work to be completed. He stated that there will be micro-tunneling rather than trenching due to the crossing of the vehicle entrance at the 24-hour Public Works Yard. He reviewed the project schedule and discussed the need for the two separate MOUs

items.title: Approve the selection of MCK Americas, Inc. (MCK), the sole responsive, responsible, and qualified proposer; award Agreement No. PRO.0181
items.text: Approve the selection of MCK Americas, Inc. (MCK), the sole responsive, responsible, and qualified proposer; award Agreement No. PRO.0181, Westside Pump Station Construction Management Staff Augmentation Services, to provide construction management personnel to assist in managing the construction of the Westside Pump Station Reliability Improvements Project; and authorize the General Manager to negotiate and execute a professional services agreement with MCK for an amount not- to-exceed $3,300,000, and a duration of three years. Mario Valdez, Contracts Manager, stated that three proposals were received and that prior to the evaluation phase beginning, minimum qualification reviews are conducted. He discussed the review process and the reasoning for two of the responders being deemed as non-responsive and not being moved to full evaluation. VP Moran expressed frustration with $10M contracts that go out without effective competitive bidding. He stated that we have not worked with the bidders well enough for them to respond correctly. VP Moran noted a similar contact was closed-out under the Consent Calendar with $6M unexpended and questioned why the other contract wasn’t used to complete the work, making the subject contract a lesser amount to get competitive bids. Mr. Valdez indicated this project is a contract-specific RFP for the Westside Pump Station to be funded by that project. items.title: Approve the plans and specifications, and award Contract No. WW-699, As-Needed Spot Sewer Replacement No. 42
items.text: Approve the plans and specifications, and award Contract No. WW-699, As-Needed Spot Sewer Replacement No. 42, in an amount not-to-exceed $10,176,957, and with a duration of 400 consecutive calendar days, to the sole, qualified, responsible bidder, J. Flores Construction Company, Inc., in accordance with San Francisco Administrative Code 6.23(c)(2), to replace sections of existing sewer piping, on an as-needed basis, at locations to be determined throughout the City of San Francisco. Aileen Caylao, Project Manager, discussed the work to be conducted at various locations, which are to be determined throughout San Francisco. In response to a question from Commissioner Paulson, Ms. Caylao indicated in that the work is for replacement of short segments, as needed, and provided examples of work. VP Moran returned to his comments made under Item 13 and questioned why an existing contract with unexpended funds was not used to complete the work, making the subject contract a lesser amount to get competitive bids. Alan Johanson, Acting AGM Infrastructure, noted the contractor had a significant backlog, was unable to keep up with the work, and that it was not a process they could facilitate. VP Moran indicated the work is for an on-going need and that the lack of competitive procurement is frustrating. He stated that as a general matter, something is missing, that the skill sets can be accommodated by multiple contractors, and that the bidding and scheduling process needs to be reviewed

items.title: Authorize the General Manager to negotiate a contract scope of work and price reduction of greater than 10% for Contract No. WW-647R
items.text: Authorize the General Manager to negotiate a contract scope of work and price reduction of greater than 10% for Contract No. WW-647R, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant Biosolids Digester Facilities Project (BDFP) with Construction Manager/General Contractor, MWH Constructors/Webcor Builders Joint Venture, to provide flexibility to use alternative delivery methods to achieve the overall BDFP objectives and scope of work, and if negotiations are successful, return for Commission approval of such scope and price reduction through either a contract modification or partial termination for convenience. President Maxwell stated that the Commission needed the opportunity to hear the item and discuss prior to taking any action, and that the item would not be considered for action at the meeting. Acting AGM Johanson introduced the item and Carolyn Chiu, Biosolids Project Manager, who indicated that construction is well underway. She stated the earlier bids received were on or below budget, but over the last few months the bids received were higher than the budget. She provided a comparison of bids received for Electrical and Mechanical Installation Package Number 1. She stated that bid procurement was suspended while staff re-thought bidding strategy and delivery approach. She indicated the need for better cost certainty: (1) biosolids project is large and complex, (2) benefits of a CM/CG approach have not been realized in this contract, (3) ability to navigate post-pandemic mark
